title: Wildberries founder Tatyana Kim steps down as CEO days after EU sanctions - Türkiye Today
html:
Set as preferred source

Tatyana Kim, founder of Russia's largest online retailer Wildberries, has stepped down as chief executive days after the European Union (EU) added her to its Russia sanctions list, Russian news agencies reported Saturday, citing the corporate registry.

Alexey Kulikov has been appointed CEO of Wildberries LLC, according to a Nov. 21 extract from Russia's Unified State Register of Legal Entities. The BIR-Analitik information system showed the appointment took place Nov. 20.

Kulikov heads the advertising agency Digiko and WB Engineering.

Kim, Russia's richest woman according to Forbes' 2026 ranking, founded Wildberries in 2004 to sell clothing online.

The EU imposed an asset freeze and travel ban on Kim on Nov. 16 as part of a package also targeting Russian banks and oil exports.

"Wildberries operates as a supply network for the Russian military by facilitating the sale of military and dual-use goods," the EU said, adding that Kim "is supporting, materially or financially, and benefiting from Russia's military and industrial complex."

The company and the Kremlin deny that Wildberries supplies the Russian army. Wildberries said the sanctions would not affect its operations because it has no assets or business in the EU.

Two closed-end mutual investment funds, Tom and Galo, became co-owners of RWB, the parent of Wildberries & Russ, with stakes of 17.5% and 12.5%, after registration on Nov. 19.

Wildberries LLC's stake fell to 45% from 65%, and Stinn LLC's to 25% from 35%.

The company said the move aimed to optimize assets in Russia and other markets under "a new concept for the distribution of responsibility and the composition of founders."

Ukraine struck Wildberries logistics centers with drones this year.

Russia's Finance Ministry has expanded support for sellers on Wildberries and Ozon hit by drone and missile attacks to include businesses losing more than 5% of annual revenue.

U.S. Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby this week cited strikes on civilian infrastructure "such as Wildberries" as counterproductive, as Kim stepped down from Wildberries.
summary: Russia’s largest online retailer has named Alexey Kulikov as chief executive, according to Russian registry data.
